task: Fix two episode-extractor correctness defects: work-log prose beating the staged diff for metrics.files_changed (#3617), and event ids that are neither unique nor contiguous because a multi-pattern line burns an index and post-assignment filtering leaves gaps (#3633).

events.content: Reproduced both defects with an end-to-end probe against a temporary git repo. On the JSON session path a work log quoting 'Linting: 2 files, 0 issues' set metrics.files_changed to 2 while the staged diff held 5 files. On the markdown path the line 'commit abc1234 failed to apply' produced a single event with id e002, dropping the commit event and burning index 1.

Measured the corpus before choosing a fix. Across 1000 session logs producing 301 episodes, 83 of 3513 work-log lines (2.4 percent) match more than one event pattern, silently dropping 71 error and 12 commit events. One shipped episode carries non-contiguous ids and none carry duplicates.

Found the second cause of non-contiguity: _filter_markdown_events drops error events after ids are already assigned, so filtering alone can leave a gap even when parse_events is correct. That ruled out fixing parse_events alone.

Rewrote parse_events to use a nested add(evt_type, content) closure that increments and appends atomically, mirroring the already-correct json_events pattern. A line matching several patterns now yields one event per match instead of one event with a burned counter.

Added _renumber_events and called it immediately before _link_sequential_events, the single call site. Numbering the final list makes duplicate and non-contiguous ids unrepresentable rather than merely detectable. Safe because the causal linker resets and rebuilds every edge by id from that same list, so no reference can dangle.

Inverted the files_changed precedence so the staged diff is primary and work-log prose is the fallback, matching the split _collect_shas already applies to SHAs. Removed the falsy guard that let any 'N files' phrase suppress the correct staged figure.

Added nine tests covering positive, negative, and edge cases: burned index, duplicate ids, empty list, non-dict entry, padding past nine, multi-pattern line, staged beats prose, prose still applies when nothing is staged, and zero when neither source has a count.

Ran the negative control by swapping in the 95da12691 version of the extractor. Seven of the nine new tests failed, confirming each is load-bearing. The two that passed on both sides are the fallback invariants, which is the correct shape: they prove the precedence flip did not over-tighten and remove the prose path entirely.

Regenerated the copilot mirror with build/scripts/generate_skills.py and confirmed the canonical and generated copies are byte-identical. Bumped .claude/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and src/copilot-cli/.claude-plugin/plugin.json to the same strictly-greater 0.6.171 per the parity gate.

Issue #3633 asks for two things and only the second is reachable: _renumber_events already makes duplicate and non-contiguous ids unrepresentable on the write path, so a pre-write uniqueness check would be dead code. The reachable half is detection at rest, for files that never pass through the extractor again after a hand edit or a merge-conflict resolution. Added --validate over a file or directory, exiting 2 on a duplicate id, a gap, a missing id, a non-object event, a non-list events field, or unreadable JSON.

An earlier corpus probe reported 0 duplicate and 0 non-contiguous ids across 301 episodes and I acted on that, concluding the at-rest validator was unmerited. The probe was broken: it filtered ids with isinstance(i, int) but episode ids are strings, so the list was always empty and the contiguity check never ran. Running the real validator instead found 4 violations on its first pass, all in episode-2026-05-31-session-1857.json, the exact file the issue names. Lesson: run the real implementation over the corpus rather than writing a separate probe.

Repaired episode-2026-05-31-session-1857.json, which shipped ids e002-e005 where e001-e004 belong. All four caused_by and leads_to edges are empty and the ids appear nowhere else in the file, so renumbering is lossless: a 4-line diff. The store now validates clean at 302 files, 0 violations.

Requirement 2 of the issue is to add the check to whatever validates episode files in CI. Traced the gates: memory-validation.yml has no episode path filter, and pytest.yml gates its whole test job behind a dorny/paths-filter whose python entry is '**/*.py'. An episode-only PR, exactly the hand-edit population the issue names, matches neither and skips the job, so the new store-clean pin would never have fired against it. Added '.agents/memory/episodes/**' to that filter, which already carries non-Python inputs (uv.lock, lefthook.yml, .config/wt.toml) and is therefore the set of inputs that change Python test outcomes, not the set of Python files.

Three negative controls, all confirmed. Reverting the data repair fails the store-clean pin with the original 'event 1 has id e002, expected e001' message. Parking validate_event_ids fails 10 of the 14 new tests. Removing the paths-filter entry fails the wiring test. With everything restored, 886 tests pass across tests/skills/memory, tests/ci, and .claude/skills/memory/tests. mypy clean on all four changed Python files; portability gate exit 0 with no drift.
